name: Malaysia

official.guidance: The Malaysian Immigration Department (imi.gov.my) states, for Multiple Entry Visa social-visit applicants from India and China, that 'the applicant must show proof of sufficient funds for staying in Malaysia' — no fixed amount is published. Separately, the official eVisa portal (malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my) advises that on arrival travellers must be able to present sufficient funds (cash, traveller's cheque, debit/credit card, or a Malaysian-government-recognised e-wallet) to cover expenses during the stay, again without a stated minimum figure.

community.typical_approved: Widely repeated travel-agency and forum guidance suggests budgeting roughly USD 50 (about MYR 210) per day of stay as a rule of thumb, and some sources cite immigration officers occasionally checking for cash equivalent to about MYR 500 per person on arrival. For Indian applicants, third-party visa-agency sites commonly cite a bank statement (last 3-6 months) showing a balance of roughly INR 30,000 for an individual or INR 60,000 for a family as generally accepted, with travellers who have fully prepaid accommodation and transport needing less. None of these figures come from Malaysian government sources — treat them as anecdotal planning guidance, not a rule.
community.notes: Reports are anecdotal, drawn from travel-agency blogs, forum threads, and applicant trip reports; they are not a guarantee of approval or entry, and immigration officers retain discretion at the checkpoint.

documents: bank statement covering the last 3-6 months
proof of accommodation (hotel booking or invitation letter)
sufficient funds presentable at arrival (cash, traveller's cheque, debit/credit card, or recognised e-wallet)
income tax returns or salary slips (for visa-required nationalities applying at a Malaysian mission)
red_flags: large lump-sum deposit made into the account shortly before applying
bank statement showing no regular income or transaction history
funds borrowed just for the application and withdrawn soon after
no proof of onward travel or accommodation to support the claimed length of stay
